source: Census of India 2011 (age structure, slum population) + NFHS-5 2019-21 district fact sheets (wealth quintile). Hand-transcribed; see data/dc-urs/socio-sources.json for the per-value citations.
method: Equal-weighted composite on a 0-10 scale of four shares, each normalised against a fixed ceiling: 65+ /0.15, under-5 /0.15, lowest wealth quintile /0.4, slum /0.4. Ceilings are plausible-range values for Indian urban districts, NOT the max over these three — a max over three units makes the worst of them 1.0 by construction and rescores every ward when a fourth is added.
caveat: TWO LIMITATIONS, both structural. (1) Vintage: age structure and slum share can only come from a census, and India's last was 2011 — the 2021 round was deferred to Census 2027. NFHS-5 is current but is a health survey and carries neither variable. (2) Resolution: these are DISTRICT figures. The three wards sit in three different districts so the values do vary between them, but a ward inherits its district's average and within-district variation is invisible.
